pl-l4d18c5-d1e115.summary: Adds that this does not deny that priests were given power to forgive and retain sins, since the Truth plainly teaches it in the Gospel.
claims: Priests have power to forgive and retain sins.

pl-l4d18c5-d1e118.summary: Quotes Augustine: the Church's charity, poured into hearts by the Spirit, forgives the sins of those who share in it and retains those of those who do not.
claims: The Church's charity forgives and retains sins.

pl-l4d18c5-d1e127.summary: Adds Augustine: priests can spare those who confess, since whom they forgive, God forgives; Christ gave Lazarus, raised, to the disciples to unbind, showing that the power of loosing was given to priests; 'whatever you loose on earth' means God, the heavenly host, and the saints confirm those whom you bind and loose, not whom you think you bind, but on whom you exercise the work of justice or mercy.
claims: Heaven confirms the priests' just binding and loosing.

pl-l4d18c5-d1e143.summary: Adds Augustine: when sins are forgiven to one truly converted, they are forgiven by those to whom he is joined by true conversion; the Holy Spirit forgives them, given to all the saints joined by charity; and they are retained by those from whom he is separated by depravity. Lombard notes that he says sins are forgiven or retained by holy men, yet says the Spirit forgives them.
claims: Sins are forgiven by the saints and by the Spirit.
Sins are retained by separation from the saints.

pl-l4d18c5-d1e152.summary: Notes, as more worthy of consideration, that Augustine also says God forgives sins only by himself or through his saints: God gives the sacrament of grace even through the wicked, but grace itself only by himself or his saints; so he forgives sins by himself or through the members of the dove, to whom he said 'if you forgive anyone'.
claims: Grace is given only by God or through the saints.
The sacrament may be given through the wicked.

pl-l4d18c5-d1e161.summary: Notes how varied the doctors' teaching is, and asks what to hold in such variety.

pl-l4d18c5-d1e164.summary: Answers that we can say and think that God alone forgives and retains sins, and yet gave the Church power to bind and loose; but he binds and looses one way, the Church another. He alone by himself forgives sin in such a way that he cleanses the soul from inner stain and looses it from the debt of eternal death.
claims: God alone forgives sins, yet the Church has power to bind and loose.
God alone cleanses the soul and remits eternal death.

pl-l4d18c5.summary: Yet priests' power to forgive and retain sins is not denied, since the Gospel plainly teaches it. Augustine says the Church's charity, poured out by the Spirit, forgives the sins of those who share in it and retains those of others; priests can spare those who confess, and whom they forgive, God forgives, as Christ gave Lazarus to be unbound; sins are forgiven or retained by the saints, yet the Spirit forgives them; God gives the sacrament of grace even through the wicked but grace itself only through himself or his saints. Faced with this variety, Lombard holds that God alone forgives and retains sins, yet gave the Church power to bind and loose, but God and the Church do so differently: God by himself cleanses the soul's inner stain and remits the debt of eternal death.
claims: Priests have power to forgive and retain sins.
The Church's charity forgives the sins of those who share in it.
God alone forgives and retains sins, yet gave the Church power to bind and loose.
God and the Church bind and loose in different ways.
